discoveries:
- In a project that has every file but no lock yet (the state a copy is in when its task runs), `gov release --lock-from` with the genuine `v1.4.0` source writes the lock today for any role. That state is the setup for the `--lock-from` role cases, so the refusal can only come from the role check.
- The first version of the W1-39 rewrite added `README.md` and `src/app.py`. Doctor's `path_map` part failed on those two files (they are unclassified), which had nothing to do with the case, so the never-installed project now holds only its overlay.
risks:
- R2-F2 checks only the lock. Inside a project, a lock with its release entries removed looks the same as a lock from a source that never held a record, and W1-39 still accepts those. The implementation will need a second record in the project, or a read of the answers file or the source, to make R2-F2 fail. That is the engineer's design choice; the case does not depend on which.
- The R2-F2 case finds release entries by value. It keeps `template_tag: v1.4.0`, because that value only contains the version inside longer text; the README states this reading.
- The `--lock-from` role cases rely on running the command by hand in the copy-time state matching what Copier does at copy time.
lessons: The guard refuses shell variables in Bash write targets and `cd` before git commands. Probing through a small Python script in the scratchpad that imports the suite's support module avoids both. Name failures with `-rf`: `-rs` alone prints no FAILED lines.
